sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Revolutionary Movement & Aggressive Nationalism** (क्रांतिकारी आंदोलन तथा उग्र राष्ट्रवाद) in India.
Late 19th Century to 1947, with peak phases during **1905-1918** (First Phase) and **1924-1934** (Second Phase).
Key figures include **Bhagat Singh**, **Chandrashekhar Azad**, **Lala Lajpat Rai**, **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, **Bipin Chandra Pal**, and **Aurobindo Ghosh**.
Shift from moderate constitutional politics to radical demands for **Purna Swaraj** and armed resistance against British rule.
Formation of secret societies, **individual heroic actions**, newspaper propaganda, and socialist-communist ideological influences.
High-scoring static GK area covering organizations, founders, years, trial cases, and revolutionary slogans.
**Partition of Bengal (1905)**, **Kakori Conspiracy (1925)**, **Lahore Conspiracy Case (1929)**, and Chittagong Armoury Raid (1930).

items.title: 1. Rise of Aggressive Nationalism (Lal-Bal-Pal Era)
items.content:
• Emerged as a reaction to British apathy, famines, and Lord Curzon's reactionary policies like the **Partition of Bengal (1905)**.
• Spearheaded by the extremist trio: **Lala Lajpat Rai** (Punjab), **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** (Maharashtra), and **Bipin Chandra Pal** (Bengal).
• Promoted **Swadeshi** (indigenous goods), **Boycott** of foreign goods, National Education, and Passive Resistance.
• **Mnemonic:** **LLB** = **L**ala Lajpat Rai, **L**okmanya Tilak, **B**ipin Chandra Pal.

items.title: 2. First Phase of Revolutionary Movement (1905–1918)
items.content:
• Focused on secret societies, assassinations of unpopular British officials, and organizing youth.
• **Anushilan Samiti** and **Jugantar** in Bengal; **Abhinav Bharat** in Maharashtra founded by **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar** (1904).
• **Muzaffarpur Conspiracy (1908):** **Prafulla Chaki** and **Khudiram Bose** attempted to kill Judge Kingsford.
• **Delhi-Lahore Conspiracy (1912):** **Rash Behari Bose** and **Sachindra Nath Sanyal** threw a bomb at Viceroy Lord Hardinge.

items.title: 3. Second Phase and Socialist Shift (1924–1934)
items.content:
• Post-Non-Cooperation Movement disillusionment led to the formation of the **Hindustan Republican Association (HRA)** in **1924** at Kanpur.
• Founders included **Sachindra Nath Sanyal**, **Ram Prasad Bismil**, and **Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee**.
• Renamed to **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)** in **1928** at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi, under the ideological guidance of **Bhagat Singh** and **Chandrashekhar Azad**.
• **Mnemonic for HRA to HSRA:** **'Add S for Socialism in 1928'** (HRA founded in 1924, added Socialist in 1928).

items.title: 4. Major Revolutionary Actions and Conspiracies
items.content:
• **Kakori Train Robbery (August 9, 1925):** HRA members looted government treasury near Lucknow. **Ram Prasad Bismil**, **Ashfaqulla Khan**, **Roshan Singh**, and **Rajendra Lahiri** were hanged.
• **Saunders Assassination (Lahore, 1928):** **Bhagat Singh**, **Rajguru**, and **Chandrashekhar Azad** shot British police officer Saunders to avenge the death of **Lala Lajpat Rai**.
• **Central Assembly Bomb Case (April 8, 1929):** **Bhagat Singh** and **Batukeshwar Dutt** threw low-intensity bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly to 'make the deaf hear'.

items.title: 5. Chittagong Armoury Raid and Women Revolutionaries
items.content:
• **Chittagong Armoury Raid (April 18, 1930):** Led by **Surya Sen** (Masterda) along with Indian Republican Army, targeting police and auxiliary force armories.
• Active participation of women revolutionaries: **Pritilata Waddedar** (led European Club attack), **Kalpana Dutt**, and **Bina Das** (shot Governor of Bengal in 1932).
• **Mnemonic for Chittagong Heroes:** **PSC** = **P**ritilata, **S**urya Sen, **C**alpana Dutt.

items.definition: Remember **L-B-P** for **L**ala Lajpat Rai (Punjab), **B**al Gangadhar Tilak (Bombay/Maharashtra), and **B**ipin Chandra Pal (Bengal). They represented the aggressive nationalist stance during the 1905 Swadeshi Movement.
Remember **'25 loot, 27 execution'** — The Kakori train robbery occurred in **1925**, and the four main leaders (Bismil, Ashfaqulla, Roshan, Rajendra) were hanged in **December 1927**.
Remember **'24 to 28'** — HRA was founded in **1924** in Kanpur, and **4 years later** in **1928**, 'Socialist' was added by Bhagat Singh and Azad in Delhi.
Remember **March 23, 1931** — Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were hanged in the Lahore Conspiracy case. This date is celebrated as Martyrs' Day in India.
Remember **Surya Sen = Masterda** — He was a school teacher who masterminded the Chittagong Armoury Raid in **1930**.
Remember **Tilak's Dual Pack** — **Kesari** (Marathi) and **Mahratta** (English) were edited by Bal Gangadhar Tilak to spread aggressive nationalism.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing HRA and HSRA Founding Years and Places
items.definition: Students often confuse **HRA (1924, Kanpur)** with **HSRA (1928, Delhi)**. Always verify if the word 'Socialist' is present in the question.

items.term: Mistake 2: Confusing Saunders Murder with Jallianwala Bagh
items.definition: John Saunders was shot in **1928** to avenge the death of **Lala Lajpat Rai** who died due to lathi charge during the **Simon Commission protest**, NOT Jallianwala Bagh (1919).

items.term: Mistake 3: Prafulla Chaki vs Khudiram Bose Execution
items.definition: In the Muzaffarpur bomb case (1908) against Kingsford, **Prafulla Chaki** shot himself before arrest, while **Khudiram Bose** was arrested and hanged.

items.term: Mistake 4: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and Abhinav Bharat
items.definition: Abhinav Bharat was founded in **1904** by V.D. Savarkar, evolving from **Mitra Mela** (founded in 1899), not Anushilan Samiti.

items.term: Mistake 5: Bhagat Singh's Assembly Bomb Target
items.definition: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs in the Central Assembly in **1929** to protest against the **Public Safety Bill and Trade Disputes Bill**, not to kill anyone (they threw bombs in vacant spaces).
Characterized by self-reliance, radical demands, Swadeshi, and boycott led by **Lal-Bal-Pal** after the **1905 Bengal Partition**.
Founded in **1904** by **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar** in Maharashtra as a secret revolutionary society.
Prominent Bengal secret society founded in **1902** by **Pramathanath Mitra** and promoted by **Aurobindo Ghosh** and **Barindra Kumar Ghosh**.
Execution of **Ram Prasad Bismil**, **Ashfaqulla Khan**, **Roshan Singh**, and **Rajendra Lahiri** for looting government money on the Saharanpur-Lucknow train.
Established in **1928** at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi, by **Chandrashekhar Azad**, **Bhagat Singh**, and comrades.
Revenge for Lala Lajpat Rai's death caused by police lathi charge during anti-**Simon Commission** protests in Lahore.
Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt courted arrest by throwing leaflets and low-intensity bombs to protest repressive laws.
Led by **Surya Sen** (Masterda) in Bengal; notable for active participation of women revolutionaries like **Pritilata Waddedar** and **Kalpana Dutt**.
Executed on **March 23, 1931**, in Lahore jail for the Saunders murder case.
Died fighting British police in **Alfred Park, Allahabad**, on **February 27, 1931**, keeping his pledge to never be caught alive.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, memorize the exact founding years and locations of secret societies like Abhinav Bharat (1904), HRA (1924, Kanpur), and HSRA (1928, Delhi).

Questions often mix up the execution dates and places of Kakori conspiracy leaders. Remember Bismil was hanged in Gorakhpur, Ashfaqulla in Faizabad, Rajendra Lahiri in Gonda, and Roshan Singh in Naini (Allahabad).
Focus on the names of women revolutionaries associated with the Chittagong Armoury Raid and Bengal terrorist conspiracies as UPSSSC frequently asks matching-type questions.
Do not confuse the Surat Split (1907) between Moderates and Extremists with the rise of the revolutionary movement; however, both were direct outcomes of the 1905 Bengal Partition.

keyTakeaways: Aggressive nationalism (Ugr Rashtravad) was championed by Lal-Bal-Pal during the 1905 Swadeshi movement.
First phase revolutionary organizations included Abhinav Bharat (1904) and Anushilan Samiti (1902).
Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) was formed in 1924 at Kanpur and renamed HSRA in 1928 at Delhi.
Kakori Train Robbery (1925) led to the execution of four key revolutionaries including Ram Prasad Bismil.
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were martyred on March 23, 1931, for the Saunders assassination.
Surya Sen led the daring Chittagong Armoury Raid in April 1930 with active support from women revolutionaries.
